quote.text: Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet.
quote.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Emile, or On Education (1762)

stories.headline: MB&F and Maison Alcée Ship an Alien in a Box — Two Hundred and Twenty-Two Parts, Ten Hours, One Weekend
stories.dek: Named for the ship in Ridley Scott's 1979 film and drawn from H.R. Giger's world, the Nostromo table clock arrives not built but as loose components and a set of tools. The build is the point.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · LEGO for Adults
stories.headline: The Grown-Ups Who Never Put the Bricks Away — Inside the AFOL World, Its Grails and Its Regrets
stories.dek: There is a word for the adult who buys, builds and displays LEGO for himself, not his kid: AFOL. It is a S$13-billion company's fastest-growing customer, and this is the descent into what he obsesses over.

stories.headline: The Route Map Keeps Widening; the Fine Print Keeps Subtracting
stories.dek: Scoot opens Haneda, SIA reaches Madrid and flies the A380 to London twice a day — and quietly, this year, the "free" parts of travel got costed back in. Read the loyalty terms, not just the announcements.

stories.headline: A Door Opens a Crack in the Gulf War, Even as the Heaviest Exchange in a Month Lights the Strait
stories.dek: Washington struck about a hundred Guard targets and Iranian mine-layers; Tehran answered again across Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain. And then, at a summit in Bishkek, Iran's president said the word the war had not heard in weeks: reciprocate.

stories.kicker: Singapore · The Long Arm of a Scheme
stories.headline: Fifty-Two Singaporeans Are Held in Guangxi, and the Recruiter Is Usually Someone You Trust
stories.dek: The largest single overseas detention of citizens on record has a familiar shape: a Chinese province long synonymous with pyramid "capital operations," and a pitch that travels through friends and relatives, not strangers.

stories.headline: The Cheapest Upgrade a Watch Reader Owns — and the One Place the Tropics Overrule the Grail
stories.dek: A strap is judged at the cut edge and the stitch, not the logo on the buckle — and in Singapore's heat the honest answer is often not leather at all, which happens to make the category cheaper to get right.

stories.headline: Nvidia Writes MediaTek a $3.5 Billion Cheque, and the Road It Paves Runs Through Everyone Else's Chip
stories.dek: The investment buys convertible bonds; the real acquisition is a standard. MediaTek's custom silicon will now plug into Nvidia's rack over NVLink Fusion — which is to say, over Nvidia's toll road.

stories.headline: Sennheiser's Flagship Buds Ship With a Feature No Rival Dares: a Battery You Can Replace
stories.dek: The Momentum True Wireless 5 lands at the same price as the last generation. The news isn't the driver or the codec — it's that the cells, in the buds and the case both, are meant to be swapped, not landfilled.

stories.headline: Venice Keeps Its Lion a Week Longer, a Country Song Passes Old Town Road, and Spider-Man Will Not Move
stories.dek: The 83rd festival is mid-run, not decided — its awards land on 12 September. Meanwhile a twenty-week No. 1 rewrites the Hot 100 record book, and the box office stays exactly where it was.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Tween Years
stories.headline: The Study Says It May Be When They Start, Not Whether They Have an Account
stories.dek: A new Australian cohort finds the age of first social-media use predicts anxiety and depression more strongly than simply having a profile. For a Sec 1 parent, that turns the whole question from "if" into "not yet."

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Portfolio Lens
stories.headline: A Hundred and Sixty-Two Thousand Jobs Land Like a Slammed Door, and the Hike Debate Reopens
stories.dek: August payrolls came in at roughly three times what was expected. Yields rose, the dollar firmed, and gold and bitcoin gave a little back — good news for the economy reading, for now, as bad news for duration and the alternatives.

stories.headline: The Grip That Predicts the Years — and Why It's a Marker, Not the Lever
stories.dek: A large cohort ties strength to survival independent of cardio. The catch worth keeping: squeezing a hand-gripper won't buy the longevity, because the grip is measuring something bigger than the grip.

stories.headline: What's Worth Booking — and What's Worth the Flight
stories.dek: A race with a stadium of concerts bolted to it, a second BIGBANG night added on demand, and a sumo tournament in Fukuoka that rewards the traveller who books early.

stories.kicker: The Long Read · The Undercurrent — South Korea
stories.headline: 빵지순례: How a "No-Fun City" Learned to Rise
stories.dek: In the most Seoul-centric country on earth, a four-store bakery that refuses to franchise has become the cheapest anchor tenant a shrinking city can buy. The Koreans call the phenomenon ppangji-sullye — a bread pilgrimage — and every second-tier town now wants one.
